contents.name: Introduction, pp. 1-2: Murnaghan's stabilization phenomenon and the displayed product table for alpha=beta=(2) at ranks 4 to 9 with the stable row
Introduction, pp. 2 and 5: the eventual-stability statement for g^{gamma[n]}_{alpha[n],beta[n]} and the definition of the reduced Kronecker coefficient
Introduction, p. 5: Definition of stab(alpha,beta) via the operator V (V(s_lambda)=s_{lambda+(1)})
Murnaghan Theorem, p. 4: existence of the stable family and Murnaghan's triangle inequalities for its support
Murnaghan's inequalities (p. 4), restated as the size triangle inequalities of the reduced support
Murnaghan-Littlewood Theorem, p. 4: bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}=c^gamma_{alpha,beta} when |gamma|=|alpha|+|beta|

Lemma 2.1 and equation (8), pp. 7-8: the finite nonnegative expansion of a reduced coefficient into an ordinary Kronecker coefficient times three iterated Littlewood-Richardson coefficients, with the positivity characterization and the degree equations

Littlewood's identity (9), pp. 7-8: s_{alpha[n]}*s_{beta[n]}=U_n R_{alpha,beta} for the vertex-operator element R_{alpha,beta}; the source attributes it to Littlewood (Canad. J. Math. 10 (1958)) and reproduces it from Butler-King 1973 (Formula 6.1) and Scharf-Thibon-Wybourne 1993 (Formula 8)
contents.reason: This identity is the exact missing joint of the source's own proof route for Lemma 2.1; this batch instead derives the expansion from Brion's formula, and the identity has no in-batch item of its own because its published proofs (invariant theory, geometry, vertex operators, partition algebras) have not been reduced to locally checkable form. It is recorded as the missing prerequisite of the escalated all-rank expansion item and needs an owner decision on whether to fund a full local proof.

contents.name: Theorem 1.1, pp. 4-5: recovery of Kronecker coefficients from reduced ones, g^lambda_{mu,nu}=sum_i(-1)^{i+1}bar-g^{lambda-dagger i}_{bar-mu,bar-nu}
contents.reason: The recovery formula is not used by any claim of this pair: the page proves stability, the nonnegative expansion, the support inequalities and the thresholds, and supplies no quasipolynomial or stretched-family application that would need the inverse formula.

contents.name: Lemma 3.1 and Theorem 3.2, pp. 8-9: stab(alpha,beta)=max{|gamma|+gamma_1 : bar-g>0} and its evaluation |alpha|+|beta|+alpha_1+beta_1; Theorem 1.2; the sharp row bound (11) for the pair (2),(2)

Section 4, Theorems 4.1, 4.3 and 4.4, pp. 9-10: individual row bounds gamma_k, the sharp first-row bound gamma_1<=|alpha cap beta|+max(alpha_1,beta_1), and the maximum and minimum weight of the support
contents.reason: These are finer row-by-row support bounds not asserted by this pair; the page only needs the single linear form |gamma|+gamma_1 and the triangle inequalities, and no scaffolded item uses the row bounds or the Weyl-inequality input.

contents.name: Section 5, pp. 11-15: Brion's Monotonicity Theorem, stab(alpha,beta,gamma), the bounds N1, N2 and Examples 3 to 8
contents.reason: Per-coefficient stabilization bounds and monotonicity are a separate refinement of the sharp global product threshold proved here; no claim of this pair depends on them, and the companion B page instead verifies the single captured coefficient directly from the displayed data.

contents.name: Sections 2.2-2.3, pp. 5-6: the Hall inner product, adjoints of multiplication, and the lambda-ring specialization formalism (sums, products, negation and the adjoint specialization X-perp)
Lemma 2.1, pp. 6: the sigma-series identities: product formula, Cauchy's identity, multiplicativity over alphabet sums, the adjoint formula sigma[AX-perp]f=f[X+A] and the reproducing kernel
Equation (2), p. 6: the specialization expansions s_lambda[X+Y]=sum c^lambda_{mu,nu}s_mu[X]s_nu[Y] and s_lambda[XY]=sum g_{lambda,mu,nu}s_mu[X]s_nu[Y]
Section 2.4, p. 7: the vertex operator Gamma(t), its factorisation and the padded generating series (6), sum_n s_{alpha[n]}[X]t^n = sigma[tX]s_alpha[tX-1]
Lemma 3.1, p. 9: Murnaghan's inequalities for reduced Kronecker coefficients
Lemma 3.3, p. 9: a sequence is eventually constant if and only if its generating series is P(t)/(1-t), with stable value P(1)
Proposition 3.2 and its complete proof, pp. 9-10: Brion's formula bar-g_{alpha,beta,gamma}=<s_alpha[X]s_beta[Y] | sigma[XY]s_gamma[XY+X+Y]>_{X,Y}, proved together with Murnaghan's stability
Identity (10), p. 10: the symmetric Cauchy-type identity sum bar-g_{alpha,beta,gamma}s_alpha[X]s_beta[Y]s_gamma[Z]=sigma[XYZ+XY+XZ+YZ]
Bound (7), p. 9: the per-coefficient range N_0(alpha,beta,gamma) of BOR Theorem 1.5
contents.reason: The per-coefficient stabilization bound N_0 is a weaker companion to the sharp global product threshold of this page; it is quoted only as history (the page's threshold theorem does not use it) and no scaffolded item asserts it.

contents.name: Sections 3.3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8, pp. 11-40: one-row and one-column generating series, the factorization lemma, hook stability, second-row quasipolynomials and the appendix tables
contents.reason: Hook stability, linear-growth asymptotics and the quasipolynomial formulas are different stability families not claimed by this pair; the page uses only the lambda-ring formalism, the vertex operator, Brion's formula and its consequences.
